tickets.title: AoC 2025 early days (medium-term goal): proofs, Array/Map/Set, friction write-up
tickets.body:
**Advent of Code 2025, early days** — the medium-term goal.
**Queued proofs (user agreed, 18 Oct; start after compaction):**
- Day 3 (Opus, medium): `best k ds` is a subsequence of `ds`; its
  length is `min k (length ds)`; optimal — for every length-k
  subsequence `s`, `fromDigits s <= fromDigits (best k ds)` (with a
  lemma: equal-length digit lists compare lexicographically as
  numbers).
- Day 2 (Opus, medium; after day 3, both may add library lemmas):
  (a) `r.repeated k n` equals the brute-force sum of ids in `r` that
  are a k-digit block written n times (Gauss sum, digits of
  `base * 10101…`); (b) part 1 equals the brute-force sum of doubled
  ids; part 2's Möbius inclusion–exclusion: no proof, a brute-force
  cross-check test on many small ranges instead. *Done* (a) and (b)
  (`repeatedCorrect`, `part1Correct`; specs walk k-digit blocks, not
  ids) and the cross-check (160 ranges, about 2.5 s); 31 prelude
  lemmas; friction (a `let` before an `if` yields an `Effect.runPure`
  term source can't write) in aoc-2025.md "Proofs (18 October 2026)".
Lambda postponing merged (`39665ae`: `List.map (\p => p.name) people`
infers). Plan
(user, 18 Oct): day 1 done (`aoc/day01.sw`, both answers right,
0.7 s; `IO.readAllLines`, `Nat.digits` added; friction write-up in

not proved: stability, totality of `Text.compare`; new default-visible

line, `List.scanl` added (`0ff412a`; user programs can no longer

write `Dial : Type`). Automatic `==` for user data types merged

tickets.title: Style: no space before `:` (`(x: Nat)`, like Scala/TS)
tickets.body:
**Style: no space before `:` in type annotations?** Consider making `(x: Nat)` / `def f (n: Nat): Nat` the default style instead of `(x : Nat)` (user, 19 Oct).

19 Oct analysis (Sonnet): recommends keeping spaces (option a). Evidence: all 335 .sw files use ` : ` (~2,665 lines); the lexer ignores whitespace around `:` (lexer.rs:344-348, `:=` is one token), so `x: T` already parses; Lean/Mathlib style guide requires spaces, Agda/Idris docs use them; Rust/Kotlin/TS use `x: T`. Switching would touch ~180 of 280 CLI snapshots and the printer (pretty.rs:264,267), with no formatter to hold the line. Options: (a) keep; (b) switch everywhere after a `stitchwort fmt` exists; (c) mixed (rejected); (d) accept both, document house style.

Matt (19 Oct): switch to `x: T` everywhere (closer to Scala/TS); record the style in docs/syntax.md. DeepSeek restyles .sw files, printer/messages, docs (not proposals/history), playground; hash_stability snapshots must not change.

tickets.title: Proof ergonomics
tickets.body:
**Proof ergonomics** (from the AoC rewrites, 19 Oct): proofs can't refer
to a let's names, so they restate long terms; an `if` inside a helper
appears in goals as `Decidable.elim (Bool.decTrue b) ...`; `List.sum` is a
`foldl`, so every proof needs `List.sumCons`; no rewrite/`calc`, so most
proof text restates terms. Candidates for a proof-ergonomics design.

tickets.title: AoC friction (days 2-4): parser, messages, proof ergonomics
tickets.body:
**AoC friction (days 2-4):** uppercase parameter names are a parse
error; error messages print fully evaluated terms (one was 10 KB); no type synonyms (`type Grid = List (List
Nat)` is a parse error; `def Grid : Type := ...` works); no
`List.zipWith3`; a multi-line list literal can't start a line with `,`;
char-pattern exhaustiveness error says "numbers other than 97 and 98";
no pair eta (`p = (p.fst, p.snd)` isn't `rfl`); recursive calls passed
as induction hypotheses must be fully applied; reasoning about `if` goes
through `Bool.inspect` with a hand-written motive; no `calc`/rewrite.

tickets.title: Lambda postponing in effectful calls
tickets.body:
**Lambda postponing in effectful calls:** arguments that perform
operations are applied one at a time, so a lambda there can't wait
for a later argument. Leave unless it bites.

tickets.title: Proof irrelevance (D1′): design decided
tickets.body:
**Two proofs of the same fact aren't treated as equal** (no definitional
proof irrelevance): `x % 100` with a hand-written divisor proof and
with the `auto` one have different types that print identically (Int
stage 6 worked around it with `[auto]` arguments). Consider proof
irrelevance for `Prop` in conversion (kernel; design note first).
Second example (19 Oct): char-pattern branches couldn't prove `c = 'a'`
because the matched char's validity proof differed from the literal's;
fixed in the elaborator with `Bool.uniqueEq` (`55c48eb`), which proof
irrelevance would make unnecessary. User (19 Oct): wants this considered, with the
literature and trade-offs properly understood: Opus design note after
multi-file Draft 3, with web research comparing at least Lean (definitional
irrelevance for `Prop`), Agda (opt-in `Prop`) and Coq/Rocq (`SProp`), and
the known metatheory (decidability, interaction with recursion on proofs,
large elimination, hashing).

Matt (19 Oct): adopt D1′; no Prop.irrel yet; remove canonical in stage 2; stage 3 on demand. Design done (draft 3, bf74b30).

tickets.title: JS codecs are about 2× slower on small inputs
tickets.body:
**JS codecs are about 2× slower on small inputs** since they became
iterative (5,000-element list: 0.3 → 0.7 ms both ways), if it matters.

tickets.title: JS encoding doesn't preserve sharing
tickets.body:
**JS encoding doesn't preserve sharing:** a result with much sharing is
encoded once per path (`echoTree(dag(12))` gives 2^13−1 objects), so it
can be exponential. Accept and document (done, DESIGN §12), or bound it.

tickets.title: JS strings are checked at every place they appear
tickets.body:
**JS strings are checked at every place they appear** (the same 1 MB
string in 1,000 slots is scanned 1,000 times).

tickets.title: Hostile Proxies at the JS boundary
tickets.body:

tickets.title: `==` operands are computed at check time
tickets.body:
**`==` operands are computed at check time.** `f x == y` puts `f x = y` in
a type, so checking computes `f x`. Needs lazily evaluated values, or a
translation of `==` that keeps its operands out of types.

tickets.title: Elaborating a chain is quadratic

the whole subexpression at every level.

tickets.title: The WebAssembly guard size
tickets.body:
**The WebAssembly guard size:** 128 KiB gives the playground about 25
levels of nesting and list literals of about 200 elements. 256 KiB would
roughly double that, with a 2× margin in Node. Separately, the parser's
stack use per level could be cut (e.g. by boxing the `Diagnostic` in its
`Result`).

tickets.title: Solving metavariables without recursion
tickets.body:
**Solving metavariables without recursion** (low priority: only large
literal values in types hit it): `solve`, `rename`, `prune` and `zonk`
still recurse over a solution. They're guarded, so a deep one is
`E-RESOURCE`, but they share the stack: in the CLI,
`theorem a : [1, …, n] = [1, …, n]` checks up to n = 56,875 with `rfl` but
only 26,875 with `sym rfl`, whose hidden arguments are solved to the list.

tickets.title: An operation's argument is computed while checking
tickets.body:
**An operation's argument is computed while checking**
(`effects::make_call` evaluates it for the result type): a closed
`print (expensive)` runs twice in the checker before `run` runs it
(`docs/evaluator-speed.md` section 6). Only needed when the result type
depends on the argument.

tickets.title: Row order is fixed by declaration order
tickets.body:
**Row order is fixed by declaration order**, so `IO` (declared in the
prelude) always comes first in a row: `{State Nat, IO}` and
`{IO, State Nat}` are the same type. Harmless, but it means no test can
put `IO` on the right of a row.

tickets.title: A misleading follow-on error
tickets.body:
**A misleading follow-on error** (found by the IO lane): after an
`E-UNKNOWN-NAME` earlier in a file, a later `rfl` proof over a handled
computation failed with "`rfl` proves an equation, but the expected type
is `runPure (bind …)`". It checked once the first error was fixed.

tickets.title: In WebAssembly the stack guard measures the wrong stack
tickets.body:
**In WebAssembly the stack guard measures the wrong stack.** Each call uses
both the stack in linear memory (which the guard measures) and the
engine's own call stack (about 1 MiB in V8), and the engine's runs out
first. So the guard is set to 128 KiB there (`crates/web/build.rs`),
calibrated in Node and Chrome only; Firefox and Safari are unmeasured.
Eliminating recursion (steps 3 and 4) is the real fix.

tickets.body:

that's a solved metavariable (elaboration only). Bounded by the term, not by

tickets.title: Zero-argument effectful calls: `IO.readAllLines ()`
tickets.body:
Matt (19 Oct): how do Unison and other effect-tracking languages invoke 0-arity effectful actions, vs Stitchwort's `IO.readAllLines ()`? Research subagent (Sonnet, read-only): Stitchwort today, Unison/Koka/Effekt/Frank/Flix/Roc/OCaml 5/Scala/Haskell/Lean, options and a recommendation.

Research (Sonnet, 19 Oct): Stitchwort's 0-arity ops are `() -> {IO} T` thunks (prelude.sw:2236-2238), needed because evaluation is strict and effects happen at application (DESIGN.md:131-135). Strict effect languages call them with `f()` (Koka, Unison since UCM 0.5.23 alongside `!f`, Effekt, Flix, Scala's convention that `()` signals side effects); monadic languages (Haskell, Lean, Idris) make actions values, which in Stitchwort would expose `Comp` (abilities.md:259). Checked by Claude: `f()` and `def main(): {IO} ()` already parse and run. Recommendation: keep the unit-argument model; adopt `f()` / `def main()` (no space) as house style; `do e` sugar later; no `!` operator.

Matt (19 Oct): yes, adopt `f()` and `def main()` (no space) as house style via a DeepSeek restyle after the colon restyle (SW-24) lands; keep zero-argument actions as `() -> {IO} T` functions. `do e` sugar and a `!f` operator: not now.

tickets.title: Compare AoC day 1 proofs in Lean, Agda and Idris vs Stitchwort
tickets.body:
Matt (19 Oct): formalise day 1 (zerosPassedCorrect, any dial size, all inputs) in Lean 4 (core, no Mathlib), Agda (stdlib), Idris 2; compare ease of proof (tactics, omega, library, proof irrelevance, ...) and rank what Stitchwort should add.

Done (ea7e7cc): all three check fully. Proof size: Stitchwort 11.5k chars / 27 helpers; Lean 5.0k / 14 (omega/simp/grind do bookkeeping but not / or % by a variable); Agda 8.1k / 24 (rewrite + equational chains + ~60 division lemmas); Idris 10.3k / 32 (no provable integers; had to hide mod).
